Event Description: The first stone tools are made in Kenya, marking the beginning of technology.
Homo habilis achieves the first likely control of fire and cooking.
Early humans invent paint using ground ochre pigment in Zambia.
Anatomically modern humans arrive in Europe.
The first known representational paintings are created in the Chauvet Caves in France.
The first ceramics and evidence of weaving are created in Moravia.
The dog is domesticated in Siberia, becoming humanity's first animal companion.
The Venus of Willendorf, one of the earliest known sculptures, is carved.
The first pottery is created in China, used for cooking and storage.
Agriculture begins in the Fertile Crescent with the cultivation of wheat and barley.
Göbekli Tepe, the world's oldest known temple complex, is built in Turkey.
Mudbricks and clay mortar are first used in Jericho.
Rice is first domesticated and cultivated along the Yangtze River in China.
The first known alcohol fermentation (mead) occurs in China.
Evidence of lead smelting is found in Çatalhöyük, Turkey.
The first evidence of copper smelting is found in modern-day Serbia.
The first evidence of cheese-making is found in Poland.
The Sumerian civilization evolves in Mesopotamia, developing the first cities.
The wheel is invented in Eastern Europe, revolutionizing transport and machinery.
Paved roads are constructed in the Mesopotamian city of Ur.
The first silk garments are produced in China through sericulture.
The horse is first domesticated on the Eurasian Steppes.
The first system of writing (cuneiform) is developed by the Sumerians in Mesopotamia.
The first known wheeled vehicle, the Ljubljana Marshes Wheel, is made in Slovenia.
The first dynasty of Egypt is established, unifying the Upper and Lower kingdoms.
Papyrus, an early form of paper, is developed in Egypt.
The first ruler or measuring rod is used in Sumer.
The Indus Valley Civilization flourishes with planned cities like Mohenjo-daro.
The Great Pyramid of Giza is completed in Egypt under Pharaoh Khufu.
The first known forks are used in Bronze Age China.
The first known dictionary is created on clay tablets in Mesopotamia.
The chariot is invented in Russia and Kazakhstan, transforming warfare.
The first alphabetic writing system appears in the Sinai Peninsula.
King Hammurabi of Babylon issues his comprehensive legal code.
The first known surgical treatise, the Edwin Smith Papyrus, appears in Egypt.
The sundial is invented in Ancient Egypt or Babylonia.
The water clock is invented in Egypt, allowing timekeeping at night.
The lathe is invented in Ancient Egypt.
The Iron Age begins in the Near East, replacing bronze with a stronger metal.
The Zhou dynasty begins its long rule in China.
Homer is believed to have composed the epic poems The Iliad and The Odyssey.
The first Olympic Games are recorded in Olympia, Greece.
The city of Rome is traditionally founded by Romulus.
The Persian Empire begins its rise to prominence in the Middle East.
The crossbow is invented in China.
Coins are first used as currency in Lydia (modern-day Turkey).
The First Temple in Jerusalem (Solomon's Temple) is destroyed by the Babylonians.
Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha, is born in Lumbini, Nepal.
The philosopher Confucius is born in China.
The Roman Republic is founded after the overthrow of the last Roman king.
Democracy is introduced in Athens, Greece, under the reforms of Cleisthenes.
The philosopher Pythagoras studies mathematics and the movement of celestial bodies.
The Athenians defeat the Persians at the Battle of Marathon.
The catapult is invented by Ajatashatru in Magadha, India.
The philosopher Socrates is born in Athens, Greece.
Construction begins on the Parthenon temple on the Athenian Acropolis.
The Peloponnesian War begins between Athens and Sparta.
Socrates is tried and executed in Athens for corrupting the youth.
Plato founds the Academy in Athens, one of the earliest institutions of higher learning.
Alexander the Great becomes king of Macedon after the assassination of his father, Philip II.
Alexander the Great dies in Babylon, ending his vast conquests.
Euclid writes Elements, a foundational work of geometry.
The Mauryan Empire under Ashoka the Great flourishes in India.
Glassblowing is invented by Syrian craftsmen in Babylonia.
Qin Shi Huang unifies China and begins construction of the Great Wall.
Hannibal of Carthage crosses the Alps with elephants to invade Italy.
Paper is invented in China during the Han Dynasty.
Rome destroys Carthage, ending the Punic Wars and securing Mediterranean dominance.
Julius Caesar is born in Rome.
The slave rebellion led by Spartacus begins in the Roman Republic.
Julius Caesar is assassinated by a group of Roman senators.
Octavian is granted the title Augustus, marking the end of the Roman Republic and the beginning of the Roman Empire.
Jesus Christ is born in Bethlehem (widely accepted date).
The aeolipile, a simple steam turbine, is described by Hero of Alexandria.
Jesus Christ is crucified in Jerusalem.
The Great Fire of Rome occurs, which Emperor Nero blames on Christians.
Roman armies under Titus destroy the Second Temple in Jerusalem.
Mount Vesuvius erupts, destroying the Roman cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum.
The Colosseum is completed in Rome.
Cai Lun is credited with standardizing paper production in China.
Construction begins on Hadrian's Wall in Roman Britain.
The seismometer is invented in Han Dynasty China by Zhang Heng.
The Han Dynasty collapses, leading to the Three Kingdoms period in China.
The Roman Empire is divided into Eastern and Western halves by Emperor Diocletian.
Emperor Constantine issues the Edict of Milan, granting religious tolerance to Christians in the Roman Empire.
The First Council of Nicaea establishes the core tenets of Christian orthodoxy.
Constantine the Great moves the capital of the Roman Empire to Constantinople.
The Roman Empire is permanently split into the Eastern and Western Roman Empires.
The rust-resistant Iron pillar of Delhi is constructed in India.
The Visigoths, led by Alaric, sack the city of Rome.
The Vandals sack Rome, contributing to the Western Empire's decline.
The last Western Roman Emperor, Romulus Augustulus, is deposed, marking the fall of the Western Roman Empire.
Justinian I becomes emperor of the Byzantine (Eastern Roman) Empire.
The Academy in Athens, founded by Plato, is closed by Emperor Justinian.
The Hagia Sophia cathedral is completed in Constantinople under Justinian I.
The Prophet Muhammad, founder of Islam, is born in Mecca.
Toilet paper is first mentioned in use in Sui Dynasty China.
The horse collar is developed in China, revolutionizing agriculture.
The Tang Dynasty is established in China, beginning a golden age of culture and innovation.
The toothbrush is invented in Tang Dynasty China.
The Prophet Muhammad migrates from Mecca to Medina (the Hijra), marking the beginning of the Islamic calendar.
The Prophet Muhammad dies, leading to the establishment of the first Caliphate.
Porcelain is invented by Chinese artists during the Tang Dynasty.
Greek fire, an incendiary weapon, is invented in the Byzantine Empire.
Muslim forces cross the Strait of Gibraltar and begin the conquest of the Iberian Peninsula.
Charles Martel's Frankish army defeats Muslim invaders at the Battle of Tours, halting their advance into Europe.
Vikings raid the monastery at Lindisfarne, marking the beginning of the Viking Age in Europe.
Charlemagne is crowned Emperor of the Romans by Pope Leo III, founding the Carolingian Empire.
Gunpowder is invented by alchemists in Tang Dynasty China.
The mathematician al-Khwarizmi writes a foundational book on algebra in Baghdad.
The Diamond Sutra is printed in China, the world's earliest dated, printed book.
The Song Dynasty is established in China, known for its technological advancements.
The first fountain pen is invented in Arab Egypt.
Leif Erikson, a Norse explorer, lands in North America, which he calls Vinland.
Musical notes (solmization) are invented by Guido of Arezzo.
The Great Schism formally divides the Christian church into the Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox branches.
William the Conqueror leads the Norman invasion of England, winning the Battle of Hastings.
The first movable type printing system is invented by Bi Sheng in Song Dynasty China.
The First Crusade is launched by European Christians to reclaim the Holy Land.
The University of Oxford is established in England.
The University of Paris is established in France.
Saladin recaptures Jerusalem from the Crusaders.
Europeans first begin to use the magnetic compass for navigation.
Genghis Khan is proclaimed ruler of all Mongols, beginning the expansion of the Mongol Empire.
The University of Cambridge is established in England.
King John of England is forced to sign the Magna Carta, limiting royal power.
The first known musical round, "Sumer is icumen in," is written in England.
Marco Polo begins his famous journey to China along the Silk Road.
The first eyeglasses are invented in Italy.
Osman I establishes the Ottoman Empire in Anatolia.
The artist Giotto completes the Scrovegni Chapel frescoes, a landmark of the early Renaissance.
The Aztecs found the city of Tenochtitlan on Lake Texcoco.
The Black Death pandemic arrives in Europe, eventually killing a third of the population.
The Ming Dynasty is established in China, overthrowing Mongol rule.
The Medici Bank is established in Florence, fueling the Renaissance.
Chinese admiral Zheng He begins his series of seven major naval expeditions.
The use of a single, consistent light source in painting is pioneered by Masaccio.
Joan of Arc leads the French army to victory at the Siege of Orléans.
Jan van Eyck paints The Arnolfini Portrait, a masterpiece of the Northern Renaissance.
Filippo Brunelleschi completes the dome of the Florence Cathedral.
Johannes Gutenberg invents the printing press with movable type in Mainz, Germany.
The Ottoman Empire, under Sultan Mehmed II, conquers Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire.
The Gutenberg Bible is printed, the first major book printed using movable type.
Leonardo da Vinci invents the sfumato painting technique.
Bartolomeu Dias of Portugal rounds the Cape of Good Hope, opening a sea route to the East.
Christopher Columbus, sailing for Spain, makes his first voyage to the Americas, landing in the Bahamas.
The Treaty of Tordesillas divides the newly discovered lands outside Europe between Portugal and Spain.
Vasco da Gama of Portugal arrives in India, establishing a direct sea route from Europe.
Leonardo da Vinci begins painting the Mona Lisa.
Michelangelo begins painting the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel in Rome.
Niccolò Machiavelli writes The Prince, a foundational work of modern political science.
Martin Luther posts his Ninety-five Theses, beginning the Protestant Reformation.
Hernán Cortés begins the Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire.
Ferdinand Magellan's expedition completes the first circumnavigation of the Earth.
Francisco Pizarro completes the Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire.
Nicolaus Copernicus publishes On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres, proposing a heliocentric model of the universe.
The Council of Trent begins, marking the start of the Catholic Counter-Reformation.
Elizabeth I becomes Queen of England, beginning the Elizabethan era.
William Shakespeare is born in Stratford-upon-Avon, England.
Gerardus Mercator creates the Mercator projection map, revolutionizing navigation.
Pope Gregory XIII introduces the Gregorian calendar.
The English fleet defeats the Spanish Armada, preventing an invasion of England.
Opera is invented by Jacopo Peri with his work Dafne.
The British East India Company is founded, becoming a major force in global trade and colonialism.
The Dutch East India Company is established, the first multinational corporation.
The Tokugawa shogunate is established in Japan, beginning a long period of isolationist rule.
The first newspaper, Relation, is published by Johann Carolus in Strassburg.
The first permanent English settlement in North America is established at Jamestown, Virginia.
The telescope is invented in the Netherlands.
Galileo Galilei observes the moons of Jupiter, supporting the heliocentric model.
The Thirty Years' War begins in Central Europe.
The Pilgrims land at Plymouth Rock, establishing a colony in Massachusetts.
The first compound microscope appears in Europe.
The city of Boston is founded in the Massachusetts Bay Colony.
Harvard University is founded in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the oldest institution of higher learning in the U.S.
The English Civil War begins between Parliamentarians and Royalists.
The mechanical calculator (Pascaline) is built by Blaise Pascal.
The barometer is invented by Evangelista Torricelli.
The Ming Dynasty in China collapses and is replaced by the Qing Dynasty.
King Charles I of England is executed, and the Commonwealth of England is established.
The Dutch East India Company founds Cape Town in South Africa.
The pendulum clock is invented by Christiaan Huygens, greatly improving timekeeping accuracy.
Robert Hooke discovers cells using a microscope.
The Great Fire of London destroys large parts of the city.
Peter the Great becomes Tsar of Russia, beginning a period of modernization.
Isaac Newton publishes Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica, outlining the laws of motion and universal gravitation.
The Glorious Revolution in England establishes a constitutional monarchy.
The Bank of England is established, centralizing the nation's finances.
Thomas Savery develops a steam-powered water pump for draining mines.
The Acts of Union unite the Kingdom of England and the Kingdom of Scotland to create Great Britain.
Bartolomeo Cristofori crafts the first piano.
Thomas Newcomen builds the first commercially successful steam engine.
The flying shuttle is invented by John Kay, speeding up the weaving process.
Denis Diderot's Encyclopédie is first published, a key text of the Enlightenment.
Benjamin Franklin conducts his kite experiment, proving that lightning is electricity.
The Seven Years' War, a global conflict, begins between major European powers.
The Industrial Revolution begins to accelerate in Great Britain.
The spinning jenny is invented by James Hargreaves, revolutionizing textile production.
James Watt invents the improved steam engine with a separate condenser, a key innovation of the Industrial Revolution.
Nicolas-Joseph Cugnot builds the first steam-powered automobile.
James Cook claims the east coast of Australia for Great Britain.
The Boston Tea Party protests British taxation in the American colonies.
The American colonies declare independence from Great Britain on July 4th.
Adam Smith publishes The Wealth of Nations, a foundational text of modern economics.
The planet Uranus is discovered by William Herschel.
The Montgolfier brothers launch the first manned hot air balloon flight in Paris.
The Treaty of Paris is signed, officially ending the American Revolutionary War.
The United States Constitution is written in Philadelphia.
The French Revolution begins with the storming of the Bastille.
The first sewing machine is invented by Thomas Saint.
The Bill of Rights is added to the U.S. Constitution.
The modern semaphore telegraph is invented by Claude Chappe.
Eli Whitney invents the cotton gin, revolutionizing the cotton industry and entrenching slavery in the American South.
Edward Jenner develops the first successful vaccine, for smallpox.
The Rosetta Stone is discovered in Egypt, providing the key to deciphering ancient hieroglyphs.
Napoleon Bonaparte comes to power in France in a coup d'état.
Alessandro Volta invents the voltaic pile, the first chemical battery.
The United States purchases the Louisiana Territory from France, doubling the size of the country.
Napoleon Bonaparte crowns himself Emperor of the French.
Haiti declares independence from France, becoming the first black republic.
Richard Trevithick invents the first steam locomotive.
Napoleon wins a decisive victory at the Battle of Austerlitz.
The first powered printing press is invented by Friedrich Koenig.
Napoleon is defeated at the Battle of Waterloo, ending his rule.
René Laennec invents the stethoscope.
The first stethoscope is invented by René Laennec.
Antarctica is first sighted by a Russian expedition.
The harmonica is invented by Christian Friedrich Ludwig Buschmann.
Jean-François Champollion deciphers the Rosetta Stone.
The Monroe Doctrine is declared, opposing European colonialism in the Americas.
The world's first public railway opens between Stockton and Darlington in England.
The first photograph is taken by Nicéphore Niépce.
Louis Braille invents the Braille reading system for the blind.
The lawn mower is invented by Edwin Budding.
Michael Faraday discovers electromagnetic induction, the principle behind the electric generator.
The Slavery Abolition Act bans slavery throughout the British Empire.
Samuel Morse invents Morse code for the telegraph.
Charles Darwin develops his theory of evolution by natural selection.
The First Opium War begins between Britain and China.
Vulcanized rubber is invented by Charles Goodyear.
The Treaty of Waitangi is signed, establishing New Zealand as a British colony.
Anesthesia is used for the first time in surgery.
The first modern general anesthetic is created by Hanaoka Seishū.
The Irish Potato Famine begins, leading to mass starvation and emigration.
The Mexican-American War begins over territorial disputes.
Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels publish The Communist Manifesto.
The California Gold Rush begins, sparking mass migration to the West Coast of the U.S.
The safety pin is invented by Walter Hunt.
The Great Exhibition is held in London's Crystal Palace, showcasing industrial technology.
Harriet Beecher Stowe publishes Uncle Tom's Cabin, galvanizing anti-slavery sentiment.
The safety brake elevator is invented by Elisha Otis.
The Crimean War begins, pitting Russia against an alliance of Britain, France, and the Ottoman Empire.
The Bessemer process for mass-producing steel is patented by Henry Bessemer.
Parkesine, the first man-made plastic, is invented by Alexander Parkes.
The Indian Rebellion begins against British rule.
Charles Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species.
The Suez Canal construction begins, connecting the Mediterranean and Red Seas.
The American Civil War begins with the Confederate attack on Fort Sumter.
Serfdom is abolished in Russia by Tsar Alexander II.
The first paper money is issued in the United States.
President Abraham Lincoln issues the Emancipation Proclamation.
The first London Underground line opens, the world's first subway system.
Louis Pasteur invents the pasteurization process.
Abraham Lincoln is assassinated by John Wilkes Booth.
The United States purchases Alaska from Russia.
Alfred Nobel invents dynamite.
Barbed wire is invented by Lucien B. Smith.
The Meiji Restoration begins in Japan, leading to rapid modernization.
The First Transcontinental Railroad is completed in the United States.
Dmitri Mendeleev creates the Periodic Table of Elements.
The Franco-Prussian War begins, leading to the unification of Germany.
The German Empire is proclaimed with Wilhelm I as Emperor and Otto von Bismarck as Chancellor.
Yellowstone National Park is established as the world's first national park.
The first practical typewriter, the Sholes and Glidden typewriter, is produced.
Alexander Graham Bell is granted a patent for the telephone.
The Battle of the Little Bighorn takes place, where Lakota, Cheyenne, and Arapaho warriors defeat the U.S. 7th Cavalry.
Thomas Edison invents the phonograph, the first device to record and reproduce sound.
Thomas Edison patents a practical incandescent light bulb.
Robert Koch identifies the bacterium that causes tuberculosis.

The first practical machine gun is invented by Hiram Maxim.
The first modern safety bicycle is invented by John Kemp Starley.
Karl Benz patents the Benz Patent-Motorwagen, the first gasoline-powered automobile.

Heinrich Hertz demonstrates the existence of radio waves.
The ballpoint pen is invented by John J. Loud.
The Eiffel Tower is inaugurated in Paris for the World's Fair.
The Wounded Knee Massacre occurs, the last major conflict of the American Indian Wars.

The zipper is invented by Whitcomb Judson.

New Zealand becomes the first country to grant women the right to vote.
Wilhelm Röntgen discovers X-rays.
The Lumière brothers hold the first public screening of a motion picture.
The modern Olympic Games are revived in Athens, Greece.
J.J. Thomson discovers the electron.
The Spanish-American War begins, leading to U.S. acquisition of Puerto Rico, Guam, and the Philippines.
Marie and Pierre Curie discover radium and polonium.
Max Planck proposes quantum theory, revolutionizing physics.

Guglielmo Marconi receives the first transatlantic radio signal.
President William McKinley is assassinated, and Theodore Roosevelt becomes president.
The first Nobel Prizes are awarded in Stockholm, Sweden.

The Second Boer War ends in British victory in South Africa.
The Wright brothers achieve the first successful powered airplane flight.
The Ford Motor Company is incorporated by Henry Ford.
The first World Series of baseball is held.

Albert Einstein publishes his theory of special relativity.
The Russo-Japanese War ends with a surprising Japanese victory.
The Industrial Workers of the World (IWW) is founded in Chicago.

The launch of the British battleship HMS Dreadnought sparks a naval arms race.
